nima: odd repro while bringing up magnet-30b-v2 int4 across 2 GPUs: when shard-swap triggers at a non-128B-aligned host pointer, later attention looks corrupted and tokens repeat earlier names but with byte-shifted suffixes. float16/int8 fine.

prateek: can you paste run flags + a tiny KVCACHE_DEBUG dump? sounds like a pack/unpack alignment bug.

nima: run: `./bin/serve --model magnet-30b-v2 --quant=int4 --max-tokens=20000 --shard_swap=true --kv_shard_stride=16384 --kv_pack_align=64`
KVCACHE_DEBUG snippet:
```
[16382] kv: pack(dst=0x7f9a8b1005, len=4096, align=64)
[16383] kv: memcpy to GPU shard1 offset=0x1f (misaligned)
[16384] kv: swap complete crc_src=0x9a3b crc_dst=0x4f2a (mismatch)
[16390] out: "Margaret" -> "Margaret"
[16397] out: "later" -> "Marga\u0000et"  <-- byte shift
```

alon: that CRC mismatch + `Marga\u0000et` suggests the nibble packing routine lost a half-byte at the boundary. int4 packs two values per byte; misaligned memcpy can cause nibble shift. Did the packer assume 16-byte alignment anywhere?

maya: we saw something similar in past with custom fastpack that uses vectorized stores assuming 128-bit lanes. If host ptr not aligned, stores cross cacheline. Quick test: set `KV_PACK_ASSUME_128B=0` or force a safe fallback where pack writes single bytes instead of simd stores.

prateek: thanks. two quick repros to run: (A) force `kv_pack_align=128` (B) force `kv_pack_align=1` (C) disable shard_swap. Also upload the packed blob hex around the failing offset so we can diff.

nima: kicked off (A)/(B)/(C) in CI. uploading hex dump to s3://redwood-ci/runs/4976543211/blobs/hex.txt.

ci-bot: nightly_pipeline/run/4976543211 queued - magnet-30b-v2-int4-pack-align-bisect. artifacts -> s3://redwood-ci/runs/4976543211/ :eyes: 

alon: practical root cause hypothesis: packer uses SIMD stores that write 16 bytes at a time and uses aligned stores for performance. if pointer is not aligned to 16B, the first store will write across boundary and subsequent unpack will interpret shifted nibbles. On GPU memcpy we then move the mis-packed bytes to shard and unpack yields shifted keys. Fix: ensure packer always aligns or use memcpy that tolerates unaligned writes, or perform an unaligned prologue/epilogue.

prateek: agree. mitigation we can land quickly: 1) add a CRC check after swap; if mismatch, fallback to CPU unpack/repack copy path (slower but correct) and emit SLI; 2) in packer add unaligned prologue that writes first up-to-15 bytes with scalar ops then use vector stores for the rest. I'll draft both.

nima: results from CI: (A) `kv_pack_align=128` - passing to 20k (no corruption). (B) `kv_pack_align=1` - fails quickly with same byte-shift. (C) shard_swap=false - passes. So misaligned host pointer + vectorized pack path is the trigger.

maya: great repro. can you also run a small userland C shim that replicates the pack/unpack with misaligned pointers to produce a failing unit test? makes review easier.

prateek: will do. also adding a unit that fuzzes alignment offsets 0..31 and asserts roundtrip equality of pack->memcpy->unpack. If mismatch, fail the test.

sam: small ops: 1) add CRC fallback to 0.11.3-hotfix branch so nightlies don't SRE-blow up; 2) longer term optimize packer prologue. I'll own the hotfix PR.

nima: opening ML ticket ML-7788 with sample outputs, hex blobs, and KVCACHE_DEBUG. sample failing tail: "...and then Margaret Marga\u0000et later". attaching s3 links.

ci-bot: nightly_pipeline/run/4976543212 - artifact upload complete. s3://redwood-ci/runs/4976543211/ and s3://redwood-ci/runs/4976543212/

prateek: quick note for reviewers: int4 packing functions live in `serving/kv/pack_int4.cu`, fast path enabled under `FASTPACK_SIMD` macro. I'll add an aligned-check and scalar prologue. Also adding `KV_SWAP_CRC` env guard to enable fallback.

alon: once PRs land, let's run the multi-GPU week-long burn on magnet-30b-v2 int4 with random host pointer alignments (CI sim mode) to catch any similar issues. Also add a model-load sanity that ensures pack alignment hints are satisfied when doing zero-copy host allocations.

nima: thanks team. will retest when hotfix lands. :thumbsup:
